data_source.notes: Annual gross adult-use retail sales as published by OCP (pre-tax, from the state's tracking system). OCP's monthly adult-use figures are only in a Power BI dashboard, and Maine Revenue Services' monthly cannabis taxable sales file could not be downloaded from our tools, so 'monthly' is empty. Medical cannabis (largely caregiver-supplied) is not covered by these figures. The 2024 figure uses OCP's text ($243,876,905); the report's chart label shows $243,916,065.

annual.basis: OCP 2025 AUCP Annual Report, conclusion text

tax_note: From January 1, 2026, adult-use cannabis carries a 14% sales tax (up from 10%), and cultivators pay an excise tax of $223 per pound of flower (down from $335) (Maine Office of Cannabis Policy, 2025 annual report).
summary: Maine's adult-use stores opened in October 2020, and sales tripled in the first three full years before levelling off. Gross adult-use sales reached $246.4 million in 2025, up just 1% from 2024, across 4.8 million transactions, according to the Office of Cannabis Policy. Prices keep falling: the average price per gram dropped from $12.75 in 2021 to $6.62 in 2025. Maine also has a large medical program served mainly by registered caregivers, which competes directly with adult-use stores on price. The adult-use sales tax rose to 14% in January 2026.

faq.q: How much adult-use cannabis does Maine sell a year?
faq.a: Adult-use stores sold $246.4 million in 2025, up 1% from $243.9 million in 2024, per the Office of Cannabis Policy.

faq.q: Why is Maine's cannabis sales growth slowing?
faq.a: Prices are falling, from $12.75 per gram in 2021 to $6.62 in 2025, and adult-use stores compete with a large, lower-taxed medical caregiver market.

faq.q: What is the cannabis tax in Maine?
faq.a: Since January 1, 2026, adult-use purchases carry a 14% sales tax, and cultivators pay a $223-per-pound excise tax on flower.
